description: Profound UI Rich Display File (DSPF) property catalog. Generated by skill/tools/extract-properties.mjs from runtime/properties.js PLUS widgets/layout/properties.js (layout widget + template-specific props) PLUS widgets/grid/Grid.js (grid widget). Each property entry's `appliesTo` lists the widget types it applies to (`*` = all widgets). `bindable: false` means the property cannot be bound to a program field. `template` (if present) names the layout template that originally introduced this property.

id.help: Specifies the ID of the current element. ID's are used to access the element using CSS (#element-id { ... }) and JavaScript code (getObj("element-id");).

field type.help: Specifies the type of control that is used to render the element.

description.help: This property is used to provide a text description or comment for the element.

button style.help: Specifies the style to be used for the look and feel of the button.

panel style.help: Specifies the style to be used for the look and feel of the panel.

value.help: Sets the initial value of the current element.

response.help: Specifies a response indicator to be returned to your program when the element is clicked.

menu response.help: Specifies a response field to be returned to your program containing the value of the selected menu option. The menu option values are set with the 'choice values' property.

tab response.help: Specifies a numeric response field to be returned to your program when a tab is selected containing the index of the selected tab. Each of the Tab Panel's tabs are identified by a sequential index, starting from 0. For example, 0 refers to the first tab, 1 refers to the second tab, etc.

radio button group.help: Specifies a response field to be returned to your program that allows you to associate multiple radio buttons together. The field name should be unique.

chart response.help: Specifies a response field to be returned to your program containing the name of the data point selected by the user.

destination url.help: Specifies an alternate destination URL for the control. The screen will either be submitted to this URL or the browser will navigate to it, depending on the 'redirect to destination' property value.

destination parameters.help: Identifies parameter names and the corresponding bound fields for use with 'destination url'.

bookmarkable.help: By default, 'destination parameters' are added to the URL to facilitate bookmarking. If this property is set to 'false', then the parameters will only appear in the POST data.

redirect to destination.help: If set to 'true' the browser will navigate to the 'destination url', passing the 'destination parameters'. Otherwise, the screen will submit by Ajax call.

color.help: Specifies the color of the text inside the current element.

font family.help: Specifies the font face for the text of the current element.

font size.help:
Specifies the size of the text for the current element.
Examples: 12px 2em 1vh 12pt 70%

font style.help:
Specifies the style of the font inside the current element.
Examples:

Normal Text

Italic Text

Oblique Text
font style.helpNote: The 'oblique' and 'italic' options will look the same for most fonts.

font variant.help: Specifies the font variant of the text inside the current element. 'small caps' displays the text as capital letters with the same height of a lower case letter.

font weight.help:
Specifies the weight of the text inside the current element.
Examples:

Font Weight: Normal

Font Weight: Bolder

Font Weight: Bold

Font Weight: Lighter

Font Weight 100

Font Weight 200

Font Weight 300

Font Weight 400

Font Weight 500

Font Weight 600

Font Weight 700

Font Weight 800

Font Weight 900
font weight.helpNote: Not all fonts will display a difference between font weights.

letter spacing.help:
Specifies the spacing between each letter of a word inside the current element. Examples:

4px: Positive values increase the distance between letters.

-1px: Negative values decrease the distance between letters.

text align.help:
Specifies the alignment of the text inside the current element.
Examples:
This text is aligned left.
This text is aligned right.
This text is aligned center.
This text has justified alignment.
text align.helpNote: The CSS property 'text-align-last' can be used to set the alignment of the final line of a group of text.

text decoration.help:
Specifies the decoration on the text inside the current element.
Examples:
None, Underline, Overline, Line-through.

text transform.help:
Specifies the transformation used as the default formatting of the text inside the current element.
Examples:

capitalize: Changes The First Character Of Each Word To Uppercase

uppercase: CHANGES ALL CHARACTERS OF EACH WORD TO UPPERCASE

lowercase: changes all characters of each word to lowercase
text transform.helpNote: This only affects how the information is displayed in the browser. To send transformed values to your backend program, you must also set the Text Transform attribute of the Binding Dialog for the value being returned to the program.

white space.help: Specifies how white space inside the current element is handled. The default is nowrap for most widgets. The prefix 'pre-' is short for 'preserve'.
white space.helpNote: If 'pre', 'pre-wrap', or 'pre-line' aren't used, all white space is 'collapsed', meaning it doesn't display.

word spacing.help:
Specifies the spacing between each word inside the current element. Examples:-2px: Negative values decrease the spacing between words.
2px: Positive values increase the spacing between words..

spell check.help: Specifies whether the element will use the browser based spell checking. The default behavior is determined by the user's browser settings.

ajax url.help: Specifies the content url for an ajax container.

results template.help: HTML template for auto-complete results panel. If omitted, a default template will be used.

iframe url.help: Specifies the content url for an IFrame (inline frame) element.

frame border.help: Determines whether the IFrame (inline frame) element will have a border.

theme.help: Specifies the jQuery Mobile theme to use for the button. The theme is associated with a set of cascading style sheet rules.

has header.help: Determines whether the panel has a header.

header height.help: Specifies the height of the panel header.

header theme.help: Specifies the jQuery Mobile theme to use for the panel header. The theme is associated with a set of cascading style sheet rules.

body theme.help: Specifies the jQuery Mobile theme to use for the panel body. The theme is associated with a set of cascading style sheet rules.

icon position.help: Specifies the position of the icon. If a position is not provided, icons other than image icons will not be displayed.

icon.help: Identifies the icon to display in the position specified by the 'icon position' property. Setting this property overrides the 'image source' property.
icon.helpNote: Material Icon set does not display in Internet Explorer 9 and lower.

small button.help: This property uses CSS to provide a smaller, more compact version of the button that is useful in toolbars and tight spaces.

straight edge.help: Determines which parts of the element will have a straight edge instead of rounded corners.

hyperlink reference.help: This property specifies an href attribute for the hyperlink. It is used as an alternative to the response property or the onclick event property.

target.help: This property specifies where to open the hyperlink reference.

download file.help: Specifies the name of the file to download when clicking on the link (instead of navigating to the link/file).

checked value.help: For a checkbox field, specifies the value to send to the application when the checkbox is checked.

unchecked value.help: For a checkbox field, specifies the value to send to the application when the checkbox is not checked.

indeterminate value.help: Specifies the value that renders a checkbox in an indeterminate state (neither checked nor unchecked).

on value.help: Specifies the value to send to the application when the on/off switch is on.

off value.help: Specifies the value to send to the application when the on/off switch is off.

on text.help: Specifies the text to to display for the 'on' state of an on/off switch.

off text.help: Specifies the text to to display for the 'off' state of an on/off switch.

wide handle.help: Specifies whether the on/off switch should display a wide handle for switching state. If false is selected, a narrow handle will be used.

default value.help: Specifies a default value for a field. The specified value is displayed on the first output operation. On subsequent output operations, the program value appears.

default value condition.help: Determines if the default value is applied.

blank value.help: Use this property to map blank field data to a different value during input and output operations. This property is typically used with elements whose value is bound to a date, time, or timestamp field. To specify multiple blank values, right-click the property and select Add Another Blank Value.

override data.help: Use this property together with the 'put override' property to override existing data contents already on the display. It represents the OVRDTA keyword.

override attribute.help: Use this property together with the 'put override' property to override existing attributes already on the display. It represents the OVRATR keyword.

put retain.help: You use this property with the 'overlay' property to prevent the handler from deleting data that is already on the display when the application displays the record again. It represents the PUTRETAIN keyword.

disabled.help: Determines whether the element is disabled or not. The user cannot use a disabled field in any way.

html.help: Used to define custom html in an html container.

image source.help: Specifies the path to an image for an image or graphic button.

hover image source.help: Specifies the path to an image that will be displayed when the user hovers the mouse cursor over the image element.

click image source.help: Specifies the path to an image that will be displayed when the user presses down the mouse on the image element.

alternate text.help: Specifies the alternate text for an image. The alternate text appears when the image cannot be rendered.

label.help: Specifies the caption text associated with a checkbox or a radio button.

orientation.help: Specifies the orientation of a slider or a menu element.

min value.help: Defines the minimum value for a spinner or slider element.

max value.help: Defines the maximum value for a spinner or slider element.

increment value.help: Specifies how much the value in a spinner or slider element increases or decreases.

read only.help: Defines whether the current element is read only or not. A read only element prevents the user from changing its value; however, the user can still interact with the element.

input only.help: Defines whether the current element is input only or not. An input only element is always initialized when the screen appears.

empty text.help: Specifies the default text to place into an empty field. When the field receives focus, the text is removed. This property is similar to the 'placeholder' property, but provides support for older browser that may not yet support the placeholder HTML5 attribute.

placeholder.help: Uses the HTML5 placeholder attribute to specify a short hint that describes the expected value of an input field. Older browsers may not support this feature.

float placeholder.help: When set to true, the placeholder becomes a floating label on top of the input field once there is data in the input box or while focus is on the element.
float placeholder.helpNote: Enabling a floating placeholder will alter the widget's DOM structure (by wrapping the INPUT element in a DIV element). Thus, any user code referencing a widget's DOM element may need to be modified after enabling the 'float placeholder' property on that widget.

prompt icon.help: Identifies the prompt icon to use.
prompt icon.helpNote: Material Icon set does not display in Internet Explorer 9 and lower.

input type.help: Specifies an HTML5 input type. Some types may not yet be supported by the user's browser or mobile device. If a type is not specified or if the selected type is not supported, a standard textbox element will be used.

browser auto complete.help: Specifies the value of the HTML textbox "autocomplete" attribute, which controls the browser's autocomplete/autofill feature. Browser autocomplete/autofill is disabled ("off") by default. Specify "on" to enable browser autocomplete/autofill or for further control, specify an autofill field name. See here for details on autofill field names.

select box height.help: If specified, the select box appears as a list box; if omitted, the select box appears as a dropdown.

select box placement.default: Calculated based on the position of the element and the viewing area just before being shown.
select box placement.help: If specified, explictly control where the choices will appears as a list box directly.

multiple.help: Specifies that multiple options can be selected at once in a List Box. The options are returned as a comma separated list.

set focus.help: This property determines if the focus will be set to this field when the screen loads.

auto advance.help: Use this property to indicate that the user does not need to press Enter or otherwise manually submit the screen. Whenever the user keys a character (including a blank) into the last position of the field, the screen contents are submitted to the server as if the Enter key had been pressed.

allow field exit.help: This property determines whether the field exit key (Numeric Pad Plus Sign by default) can be used to progress to the next input element.

allow dup key.help: This property determines whether the Dup key (Shift-Insert by default) can be used on this element. It represents the DUP DDS keyword.

dup key response.help: Specifies a response indicator that is returned to your program when the Dup key is used on this element.

prevent auto tab.help: This proprty prevents automatic tabbing on this element even when the pui['auto tab'] flag is set to true.

shortcut key.help: Specifies a keyboard shortcut that can be used to trigger this element.

response AID.help: When screen is submitted for 'tab response' property, the AID code corresponding to the key specified here will be used. If not specified, the AID code for the Enter key will be used.

cursor row.help: Identifies the cursor row number associated with this widget.

cursor column.help: Identifies the cursor column number associated with this widget.

changed.help: Specifies a response indicator that is set on if the data within the input element is modified.

is blank.help: Specifies a response indicator that is set on if the data within the input element is blank. The property allows you to distinguish between a blank and a zero within a numeric field.

allow spellcheck.help: Set to false to disable the browser's built-in spellcheck for this widget.

messages.help: Identifies messages used to populate this element.

label for.help: Specifies the ID of the element that this is a label for. This property will cause a <label> tag to be generated for this element with the 'for' attribute set to the ID specified.

show today option.help:
Controls whether the user has a Today option on the calendar pop-up to jump to the current date.

The special value 'auto-select' causes the Today option to place the current date value into the date field and close the pop-up automatically.

show week number.help: Displays column with the week number within a time period. Default is 52 (1 year). See pui.calcWeekNum to customise

calendar position.help: Controls the position and orientation of the calendar. The default [blank] is the same as 'right'

show visibility eye.help: Enables the visibility eye for the password field so that that password toggling is enabled.

translation placeholders.help: Define replacement values for the placeholders in translations.

error message location.help: Controls the position and orientation of validation and error tool tips. When 'alert' is selected, an alert box will be used instead of a tool tip.

error message attach.help: Controls what the tool tip is attached to. 'window' means the tip is always visible, even if the widget is not visible inside layouts. 'parent' means the tip is visible when the widget is; only use 'parent' if the widget is in an overflowed layout and the tip should scroll with the widget.

error message css class.help: Specifies a css class name to apply to the top-level error tip element. This allows error tips to be styled individually. If not specified, css class 'pui-tip-error' is used, which gives error message styling. Try 'pui-tip-info' for an informational message.

mandatory entry.help: When set to true, the user must modify the field by typing at least one character into the input box. A blank is a valid character.

mandatory fill.help: When set to true, the user must type characters in all positions of the input box.

required.help: When set to true, the element cannot be empty.

valid values.help: Specifies a list of values that are valid for the user to type into the input box. The values should be comma separated.

comparison operator.help: Identifies the relational operator used to compare data in the input box with the specified comparison value.

comparison value.help: Specifies the value used for comparing against data in the input box. This property is used in combination with the comparison operator property.

range low.help: Specifies the minimum value for range validity checking. The data in the input box must be greater than or equal to this value.

range high.help: Specifies the maximum value for range validity checking. The data in the input box must be less than or equal to this value.

validate name.help: Use this property to specify that the data typed into the field must be a valid simple name. The first character must be $, #, @, or A through Z. The remaining characters must be alphanumeric ($, #, @, A through Z, 0 through 9, or underscore (_), and must not contain embedded blanks.

validate email.help: Use this property to specify that the data typed into the field must be in the format of an email address.

allow blanks.help: When set to true, blank input will satisfy validity checking should any other associated validity check fail.

error messages.help: Identifies error messages to be displayed in association with this element.

error enhanced mode.help: If checked, allows error messages to display without ERRMSG/ERRMSGID-type restrictions. Errors can display regardless of whether format is already on the screen, and output data is also sent.
error enhanced mode.label: Enhanced Mode

set as modified.help: Marks an input field as modified when it is first displayed.

bypass validation.help: This property, typically used on Cancel or Undo buttons, specifies that the element will not trigger client-side validation and will automatically discard all data modified by the user on the screen. It represents the CAxx set of DDS keywords. You can select 'send data' to bypass all client-side validation except for field data type validation and still send all data modified by the user.

choices.help: Specifies the options for a select box (dropdown or list box), text field with autocomplete, combo box, or menu. The options should be comma separated. To specify submenus for a menu, indent the choices using a dash or a series of dashes.

choice values.help: Specifies alternate option values to send to the application for a select box (dropdown or list box), text field with auto complete, combo box, or menu. The values should be comma separated.

hover background color.help: Defines the background color of a menu option when the user hovers the mouse over it.

hover text color.help: Defines the text color of a menu option when the user hovers the mouse over it.

animate.help: Determines if hovering over menu options is animated.

highlight choice.help: Adds a "selected" value in css class for active choice.

border color.help: The color of the border used for menu options.

menu option padding.help: Sets the distance between the edge of the menu option and the menu option text.

menu option indent.help: Sets the distance between the left edge of the menu option and the menu option text.

option image.help: Defines the background image displayed under each menu option. You can specify one image or a comma separated list of images corresponding to each menu option.

option hover image.help: Defines the background image displayed when the user hovers over a menu option.

onoptionclick.help: Initiates a client-side script when a menu option is clicked. The choice value is passed to the event as a parameter named 'value'. The choice text is passed to the event as a parameter named 'text'.

remote system name.help: Name of database where file is located. Used only if data to be retrieved is stored on a remote server.

database connection.help:
Name of the database connection to use. If not specified, the default connection is used. This property is ignored if the applcation is called from a Profound UI / Genie session. In that case, the *LOCAL IBM i database is used.

See here for instructions on configuring database connections.

database file.help: Database table to use for the chart's data source.

database join.help: The Database Join specifications between multiple tables to be used for a dynamic, database-driven chart.

name field.help: Database field that determines the names by which records would be represented in the chart.

value field.help: Database field that determines the numerical values from which the chart is to be built.

summary option.help: Determines how values are used when creating the chart.

selection criteria.help: Optional expression identifying which records should be retrieved from the database table.

parameter value.help: Value for parameter marker in 'selection criteria' or 'custom sql' properties. Parameter markers are specified using a question mark. Profound UI will accept values from the client for any parameter marker values which are not bound to program fields. Parameter markers are numbered in order of occurrence, from left to right. To specify multiple parameter marker values, right-click the property and select Add Another Parameter Value.

record limit.help: Sets a limit on how many records are to be used in the chart.

custom sql.help: Specifies an SQL statement to use to retrieve the records for a database-driven chart. The last column is used as the chart values. Earlier columns are concatenated into the chart labels.

blob table.help: Database table that contains a blob for this image.

blob column.help: Blob column in database table that image will be loaded from.

blob selection criteria.help: Expression expression identifying which row to load image blob from.

blob parameter value.help: Value for parameter marker in 'blob selection criteria' property. Parameter markers are specified using a question mark. Profound UI will accept values from the client for any parameter marker values which are not bound to program fields. Parameter markers are numbered in order of occurrence, from left to right. To specify multiple parameter marker values, right-click the property and select Add Another Blob Parameter Value.

choices database file.help: Database table to be used for a dynamic database-driven dropdown box, list box, or text field with autocomplete.

choices database join.help: The Database Join specifications between multiple tables to be used for a dynamic database-driven dropdown box, list box, or text field with autocomplete.

choice options field.help: Database field name used to retrieve the options for a dynamic dropdown box, list box, combo box, or text field with auto complete. Multiple fields can be specifed for a text field with auto complete. In this case, the field names should be comma separated.

choice values field.help: Database field name used to retrieve the values sent back to the application. If omitted, the choice options field is used. In the case of a text field with autocomplete that has multiple option fields, the first option field is used.

choices selection criteria.help: Optional expression identifying which records should be retrieved from the choices database table.

choices parameter value.help: Value for parameter marker in 'choices selection criteria' property. Parameter markers are specified using a question mark. Profound UI will accept values from the client for any parameter marker values which are not bound to program fields. Parameter markers are numbered in order of occurrence, from left to right. To specify multiple parameter marker values, right-click the property and select Add Another Choices Parameter Value.

blank option.help: When set to true, a database-driven dropdown box will display a blank option before the options from the database table are displayed.

blank option label.help: By default, the blank option contains no text. Use this property to specify alternate text to be displayed in the blank option. The value sent to the server will still be blank.

order by.help:
Optional expression identifying which fields determine the order of the items. For a database-driven chart, this property is ignored when 'summary option' is used. In this case, the items will sort on the 'name field'.

When sorting by columns other than the first choice column, add those columns to the 'choice options field' property.

max choices.help: Optional maximum number of choices to provide for a dynamic dropdown box, list box, or text field with auto complete. If blank: defaults to 500 for dropdown, 10 for auto complete.

contains match.help: When set to true, the auto-complete query finds records that contain the search text. When set to false, the auto-complete query finds records that start with the search text.

case sensitive.help: When set to true, the auto-complete query does not convert the database search column to upper case before comparing. When false, the database column and search text are converted to upper case before comparing.

choices url.help: Sets the url to a Web service that returns the choice options and values in JSON format. If a choices url is used, the database file, choice options field, choice value field, and max choices properties are ignored.

use choices url for reverse lookup.help: When set to true, a request will be made to the choices url to determine the displayed 'choice' in the widget based on the contents of the value field. A 'reverse=1' parameter will be used to denote that this is a reverse lookup, and 'value=X' will be passed to identify the value whos choice text is desired.

chart type.help:
Identifies the type of chart to display. The chart type matches the JavaScript alias listed in the FusionCharts documentation. The available chart names are provided here:

List of FusionCharts Charts files

HTML5 is used to render the chart.

map type.help:
Identifies the type of map to display. The available map names are provided here:

List of FusionCharts Maps files

Specifiy the 'JavaScript alias' name, with or without the 'maps/' prefix. If this property is specified, the 'chart type' property is ignored.

chart options.help: Specifies chart options as a set of XML attributes that are to be attached to the FusionCharts <chart> tag. The format of the attributes is described on the FusionCharts documentation site: Chart Attributes.

chart overlay.help: When set to true, the Chart panel will overlay any other content on the screen, regardless of z-index settings. When set to false, the Chart panel will behave according to normal layering rules, based on z-index.

onchartclick.help: Initiates a client-side script when a chart section is clicked. The name of the chart section is passed to the event as a parameter named 'name'.

names.help: Specifies a list of names representing the data points on the chart or a list of screen element id's from which the names could be retrieved. The list should be comma separated.

values.help: Specifies a list of numerical values used to build the chart or a list of screen element id's from which the values could be retrieved. The list should be comma separated.

chart url.help: Sets the url to a web service that returns the chart definition and data in XML format as specified in the FusionCharts Data Formats section of the FusionCharts documentation site: FusionCharts Documentation.

chart url json.help: Sets the url to a web service that returns the chart definition and data in JSON format as specified in the FusionCharts Data Formats section of the FusionCharts documentation site: FusionCharts Documentation.

chart xml.help: Sets the XML data for the chart as specified in the FusionCharts Data Formats section of the FusionCharts documentation site: FusionCharts Documentation.

chart json.help: Sets the JSON data for the chart as specified in the FusionCharts Data Formats section of the FusionCharts documentation site: FusionCharts Documentation. The data can be provided as a string or as a JavaScript object through the use of property scripting.

background color.help: Defines the background color of the given element.

background image.help: Defines the background image of the current element.

background position.help: Position of the background within the current element.

background repeat.help: Defines how to repeat the background, repeat-x: repeats horizontally, repeat-y: repeats vertically, no-repeat: doesn't repeat at all, repeat: repeats horizontally and vertically.

left.help: Represents the x-coordinate of the current element. Specify in pixels or as a percentage.

top.help: Represents the y-coordinate of the current element. Specify in pixels or as a percentage.

right.help: Position of the element from the right of the screen or layout container. Specify in pixels or as a percentage.

bottom.help: Position of the element from the bottom of the screen or layout container. Specify in pixels or as a percentage.

height.help: Height of the current element. Specify in pixels or as a percentage.

width.help: Width of the current element. Specify in pixels or as a percentage.

min height.help: Minimum height of the current element.

min width.help: Minimum width of the current element.

max height.help: Maximum height of the current element.

max width.help: Maximum width of the current element.

z index.help: The stacking order of the current element, expressed as an integer value. The element with the higher z index will overlay lesser elements.

auto arrange.help: This property is used to automatically position action buttons or links in order to accommodate for converted overlay screens.

locked in place.help: If set to true, the element cannot be moved or sized.

allow drag.help: This property determines if the element can be drag and dropped.

use proxy.help: This property determines if a drag and drop proxy is created. If set to true, instead of dragging the element around, a proxy element is created and moved instead.

ondragstart.help: Initiates a client-side script when the user first starts to drag the element. Information about the drag and drop operation is provided using the global pui.dragDropInfo object.

drop targets.help: Specifies a list of target element id's, which identify where this element can be dropped.

ondragenter.help: Initiates a client-side script when the user drags an element over a valid drop target. Information about the drag and drop operation is provided using the global pui.dragDropInfo object.

ondragleave.help: Initiates a client-side script when the user moves an element out of a valid drop target during a drag operation. Information about the drag and drop operation is provided using the global pui.dragDropInfo object.

ondrop.help: Initiates a client-side script when the mouse is released during a drag and drop operation. Information about the drag and drop operation is provided using the global pui.dragDropInfo object.

tab panel style.help: Identifies the look and feel of the tab panel.

tab names.help: This property identifies a comma separated list of tab names for a Tab Panel.

active tab.help: This property specifies the initial active tab on a Tab Panel. Each tab within a Tab Panel is identified by a sequential index, starting with 0 for the first tab, 1 for the second tab, and so on.

ontabclick.help: Initiates a client-side script when a tab is clicked. The tab index is passed to the event as a parameter named 'tab'. If the client-side script evaluates to false, the tab will not be switched.

parent tab panel.help: This property specifies the id of the Tab Panel to which this element belongs. The property is set automatically when you drag and drop the element onto a Tab Panel.

parent tab.help: This property specifies the tab index of the specific tab to which this element belongs. Each tab within a Tab Panel is identified by a sequential index, starting with 0 for the first tab, 1 for the second tab, and so on. The property is set automatically when you drag and drop the element onto a Tab Panel.

parent field set.help: This property specifies the id of the Field Set Panel to which this element belongs. The property is set automatically when you drag and drop the element onto a Field Set Panel.

selection mode.help: When set to 'enhanced' the file upload control will allow for selection of multiple files at once from the browser's file selector. This is accomplished by SHIFT+Click or CNTRL+Click or CNTRL+A. When 'standard' mode is used, the user must select each file for upload one by one. When 'single' mode is used, only one file can be chosen.
selection mode.helpNote: Not all browsers support 'enhanced' mode. For example, Internet Explorer does not. In such browsers, the control will work in 'standard' mode regardless of this setting.

auto submit.help: After dropping a file, should a page submit happen automatically. Upload happens during submit.

number of files.help: This property specifies the maximum number of files that can be uploaded at one time.

size limit.help: Specifies the size limit (in MB) for each file.

target directory.help: This property specifies the IFS directory where uploaded files will be saved.

rename to.help: Specifies an alternate file name to be used when the uploaded file is saved.
rename to.helpNote: This property is ignored when more than 1 file is uploaded.

overwrite files.help: Specifies the action to take when 1 or more files being saved already exists in the IFS target directory. When set to 'true', any existing files will be overwritten. When set to 'false' no files will be overwritten. If "generate unique names" is set to true, then the files will be saved with automatically generated unique names. Otherwise, an error will be returned when files already exist.

generate unique names.help: If set to 'true' and "overwrite files" is set to 'false', then any uploaded files that already exist on the file system will be saved with automatically generated unique names.

allowed type.help:
Specifies a MIME file type (as reported by the web browser) which is allowed to be uploaded. If not set, any file type will be allowed.

To specify multiple types, right-click the property and select Add Another Allowed Type.

show select.help: When true, show the "Select Files" link in addition to "Drop files here" text.

border radius.help: This property allow you to create rounded corners by specifying a border radius.

border bottom color.help: The color of the element's bottom side of the border.

border bottom style.help: The style of the element's bottom side of the border.

border bottom width.help: The thickness of the element's bottom side of the border.

border left color.help: The color of the element's left side of the border.

border left style.help: The style of the element's left side of the border.

border left width.help: The thickness of the element's left side of the border.

border right color.help: The color of the element's right bottom side of the border.

border right style.help: The style of the element's right side of the border.

border right width.help: The thickness of the element's right side of the border.

border top color.help: The color of the element's top side of the border.

border top style.help: The style of the element's top side of the border.

border top width.help: The thickness of the element's top side of the border.

padding bottom.help: Sets the distance between the bottom edge of the current element and the element's content.

padding left.help: Sets the distance between the left edge of the current element and the element's content.

padding right.help: Sets the distance between the right edge of the current element and the element's content.

padding top.help: Sets the distance between the top edge of the current element and the element's content.

css class.help: Defines a custom cascading style sheet class to assign to the element. To specify multiple classes, right-click the property and select Add Another CSS Class.

focus class.help: Defines a custom cascading style sheet class for when the element receives focus.

display attribute field.help: This property identifies a field containing a display attribute hex value. It represents the DSPATR keyword with a program to system field parameter. The hex value is translated to the appropriate css class at run time.

cursor.help:
Determines how the mouse cursor should look when hovering over the element.

Valid options: default, crosshair, pointer, move, e-resize, ne-resize, nw-resize, n-resize, se-resize, sw-resize, s-resize, w-resize, text, wait, help.

Hover over the options above to see the cursor.

overflow x.help: Determines whether a horizontal scrollbar should be displayed for this element.

overflow y.help: Determines whether a vertical scrollbar should be displayed for this element.

tab index.help: Determines the tab order for input elements on the screen.

tool tip.help: Defines the text to appear in a tool tip when the user hovers the mouse over this element.

user defined data.help: Specifies user-defined general purpose data associated with the widget. To provide multiple user defined data values, right-click the property and select Add Another User Defined Value.

visibility.help: Determines whether the element is visible or hidden. Hidden elements appear dimmed out in design mode, and invisible at runtime. If not defined, the CSS will determine the visibility, it will inherit its parent's visibility, or it will be visible.

inline style.help: This property lets you define CSS properties that will be applied to the widget. These properties are applied inline, and therefore take precedence over those defined in a CSS class. Multiple properties may be provided, separated by a semi-colon. You can learn more about CSS properties at the following link: http://www.w3schools.com/cssref/. If you define CSS properties that are defined by other widget properties, the widget properties overrule the CSS inline properties. These CSS properties are ignored and should be set using the widget properties: 'position', 'visibility', 'display', 'left', 'right', 'top', 'bottom', 'width', 'height'

onblur.help: Initiates a client-side script when the element loses focus.

onchange.help: Initiates a client-side script when the element value is changed.

oninput.help: Initiates a client-side script immediately after any input is entered into the element without waiting for the element to lose focus.

onclick.help: Initiates a client-side script when the element is clicked.

ondblclick.help: Initiates a client-side script when the element is double-clicked.

ondbload.help:
Initiates a client-side script when database data is loaded for a database-driven widget. An object named response will be defined that contains:
  • success - boolean true/false
  • id - the widget id
  • error - an object with 'id', 'text' and 'text2' fields containing the error.

onfocus.help: Initiates a client-side script when the element receives focus.

onkeydown.help: Initiates a client-side script when a keyboard key is being pressed down on this element.

onkeypress.help: Initiates a client-side script when the user presses and releases a keyboard key on this element.

onkeyup.help: Initiates a client-side script when the user releases a keyboard key on this element.

onmousedown.help: Initiates a client-side script when the mouse is pressed down on this element.

onmousemove.help: Initiates a client-side script when the mouse is moving within this element.

onmouseout.help: Initiates a client-side script when the mouse is moved off this element.

onmouseover.help: Initiates a client-side script when the mouse is moved over this element.

onmouseup.help: Initiates a client-side script when the mouse button is released off this element.

onoptiondisplay.help: Initiates a client-side script before options are displayed. The script can change the options if needed.  The options are passed to the event as a parameter named 'options'. The values are passed to the event as a parameter named 'values'. The combo box widget will run this event any time the options are displayed. The menu widget will only run this event before displaying options if it is used as the context menu of a grid.

onselect.help: Initiates a client-side script when a selection is made from the selection list of an auto-complete textbox or a combo box. In the case of an auto-complete textbox, the selected record is passed to the function as a JSON object that has properties named after the selected fields.

onspin.help: Initiates a client-side script when the up or down arrow is clicked on a spinner element.

onprompt.help: Initiates a client-side script when the prompt icon is clicked on a textbox. In your script, use special variable 'value' to retrieve the textbox value. Use 'this' to refer to the input DOM element.

template.help: Specifies the name of the template used to render the layout.

center horizontally.help: Centers the layout horizontally within its parent container.

center vertically.help: Centers the layout vertically within its parent container.

record format name.help: Specifies the name that is used to access this grid from server code.

display subfile.help: This property tells the system when to display grid records. It represents the SFLDSP keyword.

display control record.help: This property tells the system when to display the subfile control record. It represents the SFLDSPCTL keyword.

initialize subfile.help: This property tells the system to initialize all records within the subfile. It represents the SFLINZ keyword.

subfile records not active.help: This property can be used together with the "initialize subfile" property to initialize a subfile with no active records. It represents the SFLRNA keyword.

delete subfile.help: This property tells the system when to delete the subfile area. It represents the SFLDLT keyword.

clear subfile.help: This property tells the system when to clear all records from the subfile. It represents the SFLCLR keyword.

subfile size.help: This property represents the SFLSIZ keyword, which specifies the number of records that can be placed into the subfile. However, if your program places a record with a relative record number larger than the SFLSIZ value into the subfile, the subfile is automatically extended to contain it (up to a maximum of 9999 records). If this property is not specified, the subfile page value plus one is used. The subfile page value is determined from the "number of rows" property minus the header row if it is present.

subfile record number.help: This property identifies the scrollbar position when the subfile is first displayed.  It represents the SFLRCDNBR keyword.

position at top.help: When this property is set to true, the subfile record identified by the "subfile record number" property will display in the top row of the grid.  This property is equivalent to the SFLRCDNBR(*TOP) keyword.

place cursor.help: When this property is set to true, the cursor is placed in the subfile record identified by the contents of the "subfile record number" property. The cursor is positioned at the first input-capable field in the subfile record.  This property is equivalent to the SFLRCDNBR(CURSOR) keyword.

subfile end.help: This property is used to indicate that a subfile with a paging bar has loaded all of its records.  It represents the SFLEND keyword.

subfile next changed.help: This property represents the SFLNXTCHG keyword, which forces the user to correct program-detected typing errors in subfile records. The program can cause a record to be changed so that a get-next-changed operation must read the record again.

cursor record number.help: This property can be bound to a numeric field, which will return the relative record number of the record on which the cursor is located.  It represents the SFLCSRRRN keyword.

cursor progression.help: This property determines the tab order for input elements within the subfile.  It represents the SFLCSRPRG keyword.

subfile return rrn.help: This property can be bound to a numeric field, which will return the relative record number of the top visible record within a grid.  It represents the SFLSCROLL keyword.

subfile changed.help: Specifies a response indicator that is set on if the input data within the subfile is modified.

subfile message key.help: This property specifies a field that is used to select messages from a program message queue for display. Your program places a message reference key in this field. The property represents the SFLMSGKEY keyword on a subfile record format.

subfile program message queue.help: This property specifies a field that contains the name of the program message queue used to build a message subfile. It represents the SFLPGMQ keyword on a subfile record format.

subfile control program message queue.help: This property specifies a field that contains the name of the program message queue used to build a message subfile when used in conjunction with the subfile initialize property. It represents the SFLPGMQ keyword on a subfile control record format.

header font family.help: The font face for the text inside the grid header row. To define a different font for each grid column, select Other... and specify a comma separated list of fonts.

header font size.help: The size of the text inside the grid header row. To specify a different font size for each grid column, select Other... and specify a comma separated list of font sizes.

header font style.help: Specifies the style of the font inside the grid header row. To specify a different font style for each grid column, select Other... and specify a comma separated list of font styles.

header font weight.help: Specifies the weight of the font inside the grid header row. To specify a different font weight for each grid column, select Other... and specify a comma separated list of font weights.

header text align.help: Alignment of text inside the cells of the grid header row. To specify a different alignment option for each cell, select Other... and specify a comma separated list of values.

header font color.help: Defines the color of the text inside the header row. To define a different color for each grid cell in the header row, specify a comma separated list of color values.

header background.help: Defines the background color of the header row. To define a different color for each grid cell in the header row, specify a comma separated list of color values.

header image.help: Defines a repeating background image for the header row.

column headings.help: Specifies a comma separated list of heading text for each column of the grid.

odd row font color.help: Defines the color of text inside the odd rows of the grid. To define a different color for each grid column, specify a comma separated list of color values.
odd row font color.helpNote: This only applies to text displayed in a database driven grid.

odd row background.help: Defines the background color of the odd rows in the grid. To define a different color for each grid column, specify a comma separated list of color values.

even row font color.help: Defines the color of text inside the even rows of the grid. To define a different color for each grid column, specify a comma separated list of color values.
even row font color.helpNote: This only applies to text displayed in a database driven grid.

even row background.help: Defines the background color of the even rows in the grid. To define a different color for each grid column, specify a comma separated list of color values.

row font color.help: Defines the color of text in an individual row. You can define a dynamic color for each record by binding this property to a field.
row font color.helpNote: This only applies to text displayed in a database driven grid. This property, if defined, will be used instead of even row font color and odd row font color.

row background.help: Defines the background color of an individual row. To define a different color for each grid column, specify a comma separated list of color values. You can define a dynamic background color for each record by binding this property to a field.
row background.helpNote: This property, if defined, will be used instead of even row background and odd row background.

hover font color.help: Defines the color of text when the user hovers the mouse cursor over a grid row. To define a different color for each grid column, specify a comma separated list of color values.

hover background.help: Defines the background color of a grid row when the user hovers the mouse cursor over it. To define a different color for each grid column, specify a comma separated list of color values.

selection font color.help: Defines the color of text when the user selects a grid row.

selection background.help: Defines the background color of a grid row when the user selects it.

number of rows.help: Specifies the number of rows in the grid, including the header row. When the "expand to layout" grid property is true, this is set automatically.

number of columns.help: Specifies the number of columns in the grid.

row height.help: Specifies the height that will be applied to each row, not including the header row. This can also be controlled by resizing the grid with the mouse. Changing "height" causes this to change automatically.

hover effect.help: Determines whether the grid rows will be highlighted when the user hovers the mouse over them.

hover image.help: Defines a repeating cell background image for the hover effect.

row selection.help:
Determines if rows within the grid can be selected by the user with a click of the mouse.

Possible values are:

none - rows cannot be selected

single - only one row can be selected

multiple (simple) - multiple rows can be selected by simply clicking on the rows

multiple (extended) - multiple rows can be selected with the use of the Shift and Ctrl keys

selection field.help: This property must be bound to an indicator or a character field, which will be used to both set and return the selected state on each record. If a character field is specified, the selection value property will be used to populate the field when a row is selected.

selection value.help: Specifies the value used to populate the selection field when a grid row is selected.

selection image.help: Defines a repeating cell background image for row selection.

row is hidden field.help: This property must be bound to an indicator field, which will be used to return whether a row has been hidden.

column widths.help: Specifies a comma separated list of column widths for this grid.

scrollbar.help: Determines the type of vertical scrollbar used to scroll through records within the grid. A sliding scrollbar scrolls freely, while a paging scrollbar scrolls one page of records at a time only.

scroll tool tip.help: Determines if the row number or the row number range should be displayed in a tool tip when the user scrolls through the data in the grid.

propagate scroll events.help: When this property is false (which is the default) the grid handles any scroll wheel or swipe events sent to it so that they scroll the grid, but not the window that the grid is placed inside. If you enable this property, these events will be propagated, which allows mouse wheel and swipe events to scroll the grid's parent window.

sortable columns.help: Enables column sorting. If set to true, the user will be able to click on the column headings to resort the data.

default sort order.help: Specifies the default order for sortable columns. When the user clicks a column, the default sort order is used initially. To provide a different sort order for each grid column, select Other... and specify a comma separated list. Entries in the list can be abbreviated using the letter A for Ascending and D for Descending.

initial sort column.help:
This property specifies the column used to for initial sorting. Each grid column is identified by a sequential index, starting with 0 for the first column, 1 for the second column, and so on. If this property and the "initial sort field" property are omitted or set to blanks, sorting is not initiated when the grid is first rendered.

The value may be a comma-separated list of column numbers, with the first entry being the primary sort, 2nd the 2nd, etc.

initial sort field.help:
This property specifies the field name used to identify the column for initial sorting. If this property and the "initial sort column" property are omitted or set to blanks, sorting is not initiated when the grid is first rendered.

The value may be a comma-separated list of field names, with the first entry being the primary sort, 2nd the 2nd, etc.

column sort response.help: Specifies a response variable to receive a column number for server-side sorting. If omitted, client-side sorting is used. The response is a numeric value that represents a column in the grid. Each grid column is identified by a sequential index, starting with 0 for the first column, 1 for the second column, and so on. It is the responsibility of the program to keep track of the sort direction, and to display an up or down arrow in the appropriate column using the "initial sort column" and "default sort order" properties.

field name sort response.help: Specifies a response variable to receive a field name used for server-side sorting. If omitted, client-side sorting is used. The response represents the name of the field bound to the first widget in a column of the grid. It is the responsibility of the program to keep track of the sort direction, and to display an up or down arrow in the appropriate column using the "initial sort field" and "default sort order" properties.

return sort order.help: Specifies a response variable to receive the selected sort order when the user clicks on one of the sort options in the grid's built-in header context menu. The response variable will be populated with 'A' for ascending, or 'D' for descending. This property is ignored if the grid does not allow column sorting, or if client-side sorting is used.

sort function.help:
Specifies a custom sort function that will be called. If not specified the grid will sort using built in sorting. The following variables are passed:
  value1 first field value to compare
  value2 second field value to compare
  fieldName name fo the field
  isDescending true if sorting in descending sequence, false otherwise
  fieldDateFormat date format of the field, if the field is not a date field the value is null
  fieldInfo formatting information of the field that the grid is sorted by; if the field does not contain any formatting information, a blank object will be passed instead

resizable columns.help: Allows the user to resize grid columns at run time.

movable columns.help: Allows the user to rearrange grid columns at run time.

persist state.help: Specifies whether the grid state should be saved when the user sorts, moves, or resizes columns. When set to true, the state is saved to browser local storage with each user action, and automatically restored the next time the grid is displayed. When set to session only the state is saved to session storage, so the state exists only within the current tab, until it is closed. When set to program only, the grid's state is cleared whenever a program is called for the first time; however, the state is retained through multiple renders while the program is active.

find option.help: Presents an option to search grid data when the grid heading is right-clicked.

filter option.help: Presents an option to filter grid data when the grid heading is right-clicked.

hide columns option.help: Presents an option to hide and show columns for this grid when the grid heading is right-clicked. Defaults to false.

row clicked.help: Specifies row value clicked in a grid.

column clicked.help: Specifies column value clicked in a grid.

reset option.help: Presents an option to reset the persistent state for this grid when the grid heading is right-clicked.

export option.help: Presents options to export grid data to Excel using the CSV and XLSX formats when the grid heading is right-clicked.

export only visible columns.help: When the 'hide columns option' is set to true, this option determines whether to export only the visible columns or all of the columns. Defaults to false.

context menu id.help: Specifies the id of a Menu widget used to display a context menu when the user right-clicks a grid row.

filter response text max.help: The maximum number of characters to use from a filter expression when server-side filtering is setup by the 'filter response' property. The length of the 'fltrtext' array field in the filter response data structure should be this property's value.

filter response column max.help: This is the maximum number of columns filtered at once when server-side filtering is setup by the 'filter response' property. This must be between 1 and than the 'number of columns' value, inclusive. Determines the size of the 'filter response' data structure.

show quick filters.help: Above each column show a text-box for filtering row data. Enabling this causes a header row to display with the grid. To hide column headings and show quick filters, set "column headings" blank.

show paging controls.help: Displays links for navigating to the previous page and the next page of records.

show page number.help: This property determines whether the page number should display within the paging bar.

initial page number.help: Specifies the initial page number to use when the page number is displayed within the paging bar. If not specified, page number 1 is used.

show record number range.help: This property determines whether the record number range should display within the paging bar.

show bar.help: Displays a bar at the bottom of the grid even if no paging bar elements are selected to be displayed. This can be used to show miscellaneous information such as column totals.

page down condition.help: Determines if the next page link is enabled.

page down response.help: Specifies a boolean response indicator that is returned to your program when the next page link is clicked.

page up condition.help: Determines if the previous page link is enabled.

page up response.help: Specifies a boolean response indicator that is returned to your program when the previous page link is clicked.

csv export.help: Displays a link allowing the user to export grid data to Excel using the CSV format.

xlsx export.help: Displays a link allowing the user to export grid data to Excel using the XLSX format.

xlsx export pics.help: Include pictures in the XLSX Export. This option only works for Load-All subfiles.

export file name.help: Defines the name of the download file used to export grid data to CSV or XLSX formats. The .xlsx or .csv extension is automatically appended to the name. If omitted, the grid name is used.

export with headings.help: Specifies whether subfile headings should be exported as the first row of the CSV file.

fold multiple.help: The property determines the height of a collapsed row, which is calculated at by taking the row height property and dividing it by the fold multiple.  The multiple represents the number of collapsed rows that can fit into one expanded row.

expanded.help: Determines if the rows are first displayed in expanded (also known as folded) mode.  This property is similar to the SFLFOLD keyword.

collapsed.help: Determines if the rows are first displayed in collapsed (also known as truncated) mode.  This property is similar to the SFLDROP keyword.

return mode.help: This property can be bound to a field that will provide an indication of whether the grid rows were in expanded (also known as folded) mode or in collapsed (also known as truncated) mode on input.  It represents the SFLMODE keyword. The bound field will contain a value of 0 if the grid rows are in expanded mode and a value of 1 if the grid rows are in collapsed mode.

single row zoom.help: Determines if a zoom icon is shown on collapsed rows. Once the user clicks the icon, the row is expanded. All other rows remain collapsed.

tree level field.help: This property must be bound to a numeric field which contains the tree level of each grid record. Each higher level record that has lower level records below it would be collapsible.

tree level column.help: This property specifies the column used to expand and collapse the tree levels, if property "tree level field" is specified. The default is column 0. Each grid column is identified by a sequential index, starting with 0 for the first column, 1 for the second column, and so on. Note that if this property is specified, then property "tree level field" must also be specified.

tree level collapsed.help: Determines if the rows in a grid tree are first displayed in collapsed mode.

database fields.help: A set of database field names to use to retrieve the data for a database-driven grid. The field names should be comma separated.

allow any select statement.help:
Allows any valid SELECT SQL statement.

If this is false (default), a row count is retrieved by running SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (your-custom-sql-property), so your "custom sql" property must work with that syntax. This prevents the use of common table expressions, the optimize clause, and a few other things.

If set to true, the row count will be determined by running your statment as-is and looping through all rows to count them.

Note: False performs better, but true allows a wider variety of SQL statements.

load fields into widgets.help: Allows fields from database-driven grids to be bound to widgets instead of loaded directly onto the grid

load all rows.help: Can only be used when "load fields into widgets" property is true. Loads all data at once, instead of page-by-page.

data url.help: Sets the url to a Web service that returns JSON data for a database-driven grid.

data transform function.help: The name of a JavaScript function to be called to process the results of the "data url" program. This can be used to transform data from the program into the format expected by the grid widget.

starting row.help: Specifies the starting subfile row for retrieving data from the screen.

ending row.help: Specifies the ending subfile row for retrieving data from the screen.

data columns.help: Specifies a comma separated list of column numbers for retrieving data from the screen.

grid row translation placeholders.help: Define replacement values for the placeholders in translations.

expand to layout.help: If set to true, the grid will automatically expand to the full size of a layout container.

border width.help: The thickness of the grid's outer borders and inner separators.

onfilterchange.help: Initiates a client-side script when the filter has changed.

onrowclick.help: Initiates a client-side script when a row within the grid is clicked. The script can determine the row number using the row variable.

onrowdblclick.help: Initiates a client-side script when a row within the grid is double-clicked. The script can determine the row number using the row variable.

onrowmouseover.help: Initiates a client-side script when the mouse is moved over a row within the grid. The script can determine the row number using the row variable.

onrowmouseout.help: Initiates a client-side script when the mouse is moved off of a row within the grid. The script can determine the row number using the row variable.

onpagedown.help: Initiates a client-side script when the user pages down using the grid's scrollbar or the grid's paging bar. To prevent the grid's default paging action, the script must evaluate to false.

onpageup.help: Initiates a client-side script when the user pages up using the grid's scrollbar or the grid's paging bar. To prevent the grid's default paging action, the script must evaluate to false.

onscroll.help: Initiates a client-side script when the user scrolls using the grid's scrollbar. The row variable in the script provides the top row of the grid.

header text.help: Specifies the text that will appear in the panel header.

section names.help: Specifies a comma separate list of section names for the accordion.

active section.help: This property specifies the initial active section on an Accordion Layout. Each section within an Accordion is identified by a sequential index, starting with 0 for the first section, 1 for the second section, and so on. When this property is bound to a field, the currently-active section will be included in the response when the screen is submitted to the server-side program.

small sections.help: This property uses CSS to provide a smaller, more compact version of the header sections.

allow collapse.help: Determines if the accordion can be fully collapsed.

onsectionclick.help: Initiates a client-side script when an accordion section is expanded.  The section index is passed to the event as a parameter named "section".  If the client-side script evaluates to false, the section will not be expanded.

lazy load.help: When true, render contents of a tab or section after the user activates it instead of rendering everything immediately (which can be slower).

onlazyload.help: Initiates a client-side script after a container is rendered lazily. (See lazy load property.)

layout items.help: The number of containers for this layout.

style rules.help: String of CSS stylesheet rules, used to define positions and dimensions of containers. Leave empty when styles are expected to be defined in an external stylesheet. See Responsive Layout for more information.

use viewport.help:
Determines how @media rules in "style rules" are interpreted. When "use viewport" is true, the page size determines which @media rules to apply. When false, the layout's height and width determine which @media rules to apply.

See Responsive Layout for more information.

container names.help: List of container names to aid in designing screens. Names appear only in Responsive Dialog preview and Designer canvas.

movable tabs.help: Allows the user to rearrange tabs at runtime.

legend.help: Text to display in the field set's legend.

legend align.help: The alignment of the legend text.

border style.help: The style of the element's border.

rows.help: Specifies the number of table rows for this layout.

columns.help: Specifies the number of table columns for this layout.

top bar.help: Determines whether the mobile layout should have a top bar.

bottom bar.help: Determines whether the mobile layout should have a bottom bar.
